findings.evidence: GenLoop.map_const at Map.lean:45 = `map f (GenLoop.const) = GenLoop.const` (const = argument); new HomotopyGroup.map_const at ConstantMap.lean:60 = `map (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl = Function.const …` (const = the map). GenLoop.map_const_continuousMap (ConstantMap.lean:35) shows the author's own chosen disambiguator.
findings.fix: Rename the HomotopyGroup constant-map lemmas to match the GenLoop layer, e.g. map_const_continuousMap / map_const_continuousMap_apply and mapHom_const_continuousMap, reserving HomotopyGroup.map_const for the const-class analogue of GenLoop.map_const.
findings.issue: HomotopyGroup.map_const_apply / map_const (lines 51, 60) use 'const' to mean the constant continuous map, but the adjacent GenLoop precedent GenLoop.map_const (Map.lean:45) uses 'const' for the constant loop/element argument. The name that by that precedent should denote 'map of the const class (⟦const⟧)' is consumed here. The author acknowledged the clash by naming the GenLoop analogue map_const_continuousMap (line 35) rather than map_const, but did not carry the disambiguator to the HomotopyGroup layer.

summary: Names are largely standard and describe conclusions, but 'const' flips meaning across the stacked induced-map API: GenLoop.map_const denotes the constant loop argument while the new HomotopyGroup.map_const/map_const_apply denote the constant continuous map. The author already disambiguated this in GenLoop (map_const_continuousMap) but reused bare map_const one layer up.
